senses.definition: The quality or degree of being strong.
examples: It requires great strength to lift heavy objects.

quotes.text: Our castle’s strength will laugh a siege to scorn.

quotes.text: He was thinking; but the glory of the song, the swell from the great organ, the clustered lights, […], the height and vastness of this noble fane, its antiquity and its strength—all these things seemed to have their part as causes of the thrilling emotion that accompanied his thoughts.

senses.definition: The intensity of a force or power; potency.
examples: He had the strength of ten men.

quotes.text: Study gives strength to the mind; conversation, grace: the first apt to give stiffness, the other suppleness: one gives substance and form to the statue, the other polishes it.
quotes.reference: 1699, William Temple, Heads designed for an essay on conversations:

senses.definition: The strongest part of something; that on which confidence or reliance is based.

quotes.text: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
quotes.reference: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London: […] Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Psalms 46:1:

quotes.text: […] certainly there is not in the world a greater strength against temptations, then is deposited in an obedient understanding […].
quotes.reference: 1649, Jeremy Taylor, The Great Examplar of Sanctity and Holy Life according to the Christian Institution, London: Francis Ash, Part 1, Section 4, Discourse 2, p. 66:

quotes.text: The compulsion to expose, renegotiate, or reinvent the strengths and weaknesses of dance tradition offers little in its final outcome to attract the average dance-goer.
